notes:
Comics read aloud with a cast.

A comic page already tells you who is speaking. Text inside a speech balloon is a character; text sitting on the artwork is a caption or a sign. A drawn-out shout is lettered bigger than the dialogue around it; a thought sits in a scalloped cloud. Every reader app throws all of that away and reads the page as one flat block of text in one voice.

Manga Rain now reads the page instead.

WHO IS SPEAKING. Your chosen voice reads the dialogue. Captions, signs and narration get a different one, so a scene stops sounding like a single person reading a list. The app works this out by looking at the page — a balloon is a flat bright shape drawn under the lettering, artwork is not — so it is a measurement, not a guess.

HOW IT IS SAID. A shout is read a little faster, a thought a little slower and kept in the same character's voice, because it is the same person thinking. Both are read off the drawing: how big the letters are, and how rough the balloon's outline is.

TELLING CHARACTERS APART. Optional, in Settings › Voice. In a two-hander the characters stand apart and their balloons follow them, so when the balloons fall clearly into two groups the app gives them two voices. It only commits when the split is obvious — voices swapping at random mid-scene would be worse than one voice reading everything.

SOMETHING TO WATCH. A strip at the foot of the page shows the line being spoken and who is speaking it, with thoughts in italic and shouts in bold. Read-along on a comic used to be a voice with nothing to follow.

Three settings — ONE VOICE, NARRATOR, CAST — so you can take as much or as little of this as you like. NARRATOR is the default because that split is measured rather than guessed.
